e.etymology: A variant of Adrian with an E in place of the A. Adrian comes from Latin Hadrianus, a man from the town of Hadria in northern Italy.
The English word purity, from Old French purete and Latin purus, clean, used as a virtue name like Charity and Verity.
A Spanish and Filipino surname, an older spelling of Rojas, from rojo, red. American use as a first name follows Roxas, a character in the Kingdom Hearts video games.

assoc.t: Roxas of the Kingdom Hearts video games

e.etymology: Arabic Uthman, traditionally explained as the young of a bustard or another animal. Uthman ibn Affan was the third caliph of Islam; the Turkish form Osman gave the Ottoman Empire its name.
A spelling of Jireh, from Jehovah-jireh in Genesis 22, the name Abraham gave the place where God supplied a ram: the Lord will provide. Use grew after the 2021 worship song Jireh.
An Ethiopian and Eritrean name borne by Na'od, emperor of Ethiopia from 1494 to 1508.
A modern elaboration of Ariel or Arely, used mainly in Hispanic families.
An Ethiopian name from haset, the Amharic and Ge'ez word for joy.
A modern American coinage that joins the Kai sound to the -lee ending, on the pattern of Paisley and Hazley.
A modern American blend of Laila or Layla with the -lyn ending.
A modern Caribbean Spanish elaboration of Eliana with the -is ending found in names such as Yanelis and Lianis.
The name of a heroine in the Japanese manga and anime Dragon Ball, the daughter of Mr. Satan. Her name was coined as an anagram of devil.

assoc.t: Dragon Ball Z fighter who marries Gohan

e.note: Coined for Dragon Ball as an anagram of devil; fans of the series will know it at once.

e.etymology: Hungarian Anikó is Anna plus the diminutive ending -ikó; Anna comes from Hebrew Hannah, grace. American parents give the name to boys as well as girls.
The name of Juvia Lockser, a water mage in the Japanese manga and anime Fairy Tail. It is widely taken as a play on Spanish lluvia, rain.

assoc.t: Juvia Lockser of the anime Fairy Tail

e.etymology: A modern coinage with the sound of risen and the -zen ending of Jaxen and Daxen. Ryzen is also the name of AMD's computer processors, launched in 2017.
A modern American coinage built on Lynn, close in sound to Lennox.
A spelling of Zyaire, a modern American name based on Zaire, the former name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and of the Congo River.
A Bulgarian male name, written Диян. In the United States it is also used by South Asian families.
A spelling of Armoni, a variant of Armani, the Italian surname made famous by the fashion house, with an echo of the word harmony.
A shortened English form of the Irish surname Ó Gríobhtha, descendant of Gríobhtha, a personal name from gríobh, griffin. Baseball's Ken Griffey Jr. made it familiar as a first name.
namesakes: Ken Griffey Jr. (Hall of Fame baseball outfielder)

assoc.t: baseball's Ken Griffey Jr. and his father Ken Griffey Sr.

e.etymology: A modern American name that joins Jay to the sound of Leilani and Kailani.
A spelling of Zuri, from Swahili -zuri, good or beautiful.
An English surname meaning son of Rawlin, a medieval pet form of Raoul, the Norman French form of Ralph. Ralph is from Old Norse Rathulfr, counsel wolf.
A respelling of chaos that matches Greek khaos, the gaping void that came first in Greek creation myth. The English word later took on the sense of disorder.
e.note: Chaos is the everyday English word for disorder and confusion.

assoc.t: sounds the same as chaos, total disorder

e.etymology: A respelling of Legacy, the English word for what one generation hands to the next, from Latin legatus. Legacy came into use as a given name in the United States in the 21st century.
A Yiddish pet form of Avrum, the Yiddish form of Avraham (Abraham), the biblical patriarch. It is used mainly in Hasidic Jewish communities.
The Old Norse name of Skadi, a giantess and goddess of winter, skiing and the hunt who married the sea god Njord. The origin of her name is debated.
A Punjabi Sikh name joining gur, the Guru, with naaz, a Persian loanword for pride or grace.

e.meaning: one who lives or works at a barn
e.etymology: A surname, in America usually a form of German Stadler, from Middle High German stadel, a barn or granary.

assoc.t: Statler, one of the two heckling old men of the Muppets
The Statler Brothers, country vocal group

e.etymology: A short form of William, from Germanic wil, will, and helm, helmet. How the W became a B is unclear; it may belong with medieval letter swaps such as Dick for Rick.
namesakes: Bill Murray (actor in Ghostbusters and Groundhog Day)
e.note: Also the everyday word for an invoice, a banknote and a proposed law.

e.etymology: A spelling of Ernest shaped by the English word earnest. Ernest was borrowed in the 18th century from German Ernst, from Old High German ernust, vigor or strife.

assoc.t: Oscar Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest
